label: Sausage
notes: Standard UK pork sausages often contain wheat rusk and sulphite preservatives. Verify if using gluten-free.

label: Black pudding
notes: Usually contains oats or barley.

label: Butter
notes: Butter contains trace lactose, usually well tolerated by lactose intolerants, but is still a milk allergen.

label: Cheddar
notes: Aged hard cheese; lactose is generally negligible.

label: Parmesan
notes: Traditional parmesan contains animal rennet. Negligible lactose.

label: Feta
notes: Usually made from sheep/goat milk.

label: Coconut
notes: Botanically a drupe. Not classified as a tree nut under UK/EU allergen law.

label: Apricot
notes: Dried apricots very commonly contain high levels of added sulphites (E220) to preserve colour.

label: Raisin
notes: Dried vine fruits often contain sulphites.

label: Sultana
notes: Particularly golden sultanas which are heavily treated with sulphur dioxide.

label: Fenugreek
notes: Legume. Some peanut-allergic individuals can cross-react with fenugreek, though it's not a legal allergen itself.

label: Oats
notes: Oats naturally contain avenin and are highly prone to gluten cross-contamination unless certified 'Gluten Free'. Legally grouped with gluten-containing cereals in the UK.

label: Buckwheat
notes: Despite the name, buckwheat is not related to wheat and is naturally gluten-free.

label: Cornflour
notes: Usually pure maize/corn starch in the UK. Double-check facility cross-contamination for gluten if used as a GF thickener.

label: Chestnut
notes: Chestnuts are not classified as an allergen under UK/EU 'Tree Nut' legislation.

label: Pine nut
notes: Pine nuts are seeds, not classified as an allergen under UK/EU 'Tree Nut' legislation. However, many sufferers avoid them.

label: Ketchup
notes: Commercial ketchup recipes very commonly contain celery as a flavouring.

label: Brown sauce
notes: Usually contains tomatoes and rye/barley flour or malt vinegar.

label: English mustard
notes: Standard English mustard usually contains wheat flour as a thickener/stabiliser.

label: Soy sauce
notes: Traditional soy sauce is brewed with roasted wheat.

label: Tamari
notes: Japanese soy sauce made without wheat. Always check the label to ensure it is 100% wheat-free.

label: Hoisin sauce
notes: Typically made from fermented soybean paste, garlic, vinegar, sesame oil, and wheat flour.

label: Black bean sauce
notes: Usually contains fermented black soybeans, soy sauce (wheat), garlic, and sesame oil.

label: Red curry paste
notes: Authentic Thai curry pastes typically contain shrimp paste.

label: Vegetable stock
notes: Commercial stock cubes often contain hidden celery and sometimes gluten.

label: Malt vinegar
notes: Made from malted barley.

label: Shaoxing wine
notes: Traditional Shaoxing wine contains wheat.

label: Puff pastry
notes: Commercial puff pastry is often made with vegetable oils instead of butter (vegan friendly), check packaging.

label: Soba noodles
notes: Despite being buckwheat, standard commercial soba noodles contain high ratios of wheat flour.

label: Gluten-free bun
notes: Commercial gluten-free buns frequently use egg as a binder.

label: Taco shell
notes: Made from corn, but often subject to severe cross-contamination in fryers.

label: Miso paste
notes: Many miso pastes are fermented with barley or wheat. Check specific brands for gluten-free certification.

label: Dashi
notes: Traditional Japanese dashi contains bonito flakes (fish). Kombu dashi is vegan, but standard dashi is not.

label: Gochujang
notes: Traditionally contains fermented soybeans and glutinous rice, but commercial varieties often contain wheat.

label: Kimchi
notes: Traditional kimchi contains fish sauce or salted shrimp.

label: Tortilla chip
notes: Often subject to cross-contamination if fried in shared oil.

label: Refried beans
notes: Traditional Mexican recipes may use lard (pork fat) instead of vegetable oil.

label: Vanilla extract
notes: Real vanilla extract contains a significant alcohol base.

label: Dark chocolate
notes: Most dark chocolate has cross-contamination warnings for milk.

label: Baking powder
notes: Some cheap baking powders use wheat starch as a bulking agent. Check for gluten-free certification.

label: Beer
notes: Beer is typically brewed from malted barley or wheat.

label: Amaretto
notes: Traditional amaretto is made from apricot kernels and almonds, making it a tree-nut allergen risk.

label: Oat milk
notes: Oat drinks are only gluten-free if made from certified gluten-free oats.
